profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between the Research Program Manager and the Data Visualization Lead at a financial research firm preparing an internal client-facing briefing pack based on a study about classifying ECB policy announcements by their effects on market volatility. The team has already completed the modeling work, and this meeting is to align handoffs between the methods write-up and the chartbook for four Eurozone volatility series. The agenda is to confirm which announcement set is going into the briefing, what the 'classification table' and 'final figures' should contain, how status will be reported by end of week, and who updates the shared deck and appendix files. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on deliverables for Friday's briefing package and a clean handoff between the research and visualization workstreams.

members.name: Elena Marconi
members.expertise: Quant research coordination, policy-event studies, stakeholder communication
members.background: Elena manages cross-functional deliverables for a macro-financial research group and previously worked in an economic policy think tank translating technical studies into executive-ready briefings.
members.private_state: She wants the package to look stable and decision-ready for senior leadership, avoid reopening modeling choices, and keep the briefing deck concise enough to circulate externally with minimal edits.
hidden_assumptions: The '144 announcements' refers to the cleaned event universe after excluding dates that were merged or judged non-distinct in the final research log.
A 'classification table' for a briefing means one row per ECB announcement date with a single final label and no method-by-method comparison columns unless moved to an appendix.
If a figure is marked 'final,' it is presentation-ready with branding, footnotes, and the exact date set that will appear in the briefing deck.
A workstream is 'on track' if the material is polished enough to drop into the Friday client deck without further iteration.

members.name: David Klein
members.expertise: Financial chart design, research graphics pipelines, reproducible reporting
members.background: David leads the visualization function for market research publications and previously built automated charting workflows for sell-side strategy teams.
members.private_state: He wants to preserve reproducibility, minimize manual edits near publication, and keep enough methodological detail in the artifacts so that later updates can be generated from the same pipeline.
hidden_assumptions: The '144 announcements' refers to the master event list currently in the shared pipeline, including same-day policy communication items that remain separate unless explicitly collapsed by the modeling team.
A 'classification table' means the machine-readable output from the pipeline, including labels from both smoothed-probability rules and the k-means benchmark so downstream charts can be regenerated.
If a figure is 'final,' it means analytically locked and numerically checked; branding and deck formatting can still happen later.
A workstream is 'on track' if the underlying data objects and charts are reproducible and numerically stable, even if slide-ready formatting is unfinished.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to 'the 144 ECB announcements' as if it is a single settled event set.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena means the curated final list used in the methods memo, where a few same-day communications were collapsed into one announcement date for briefing simplicity.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: David means the current master pipeline list totaling 144 entries, where same-day communications still appear as separate event objects unless explicitly merged downstream.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both use the same total count and the same phrase, so the shared number creates false confidence that they are referencing the identical set; neither expects that different construction rules could still yield '144 announcements.'

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that David will deliver the 'classification table' for the deck and appendix.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena expects a compact briefing artifact containing date, market, and one final up/down/no-effect label per announcement, with benchmark-method detail excluded from the main handoff.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: David expects to hand over the full analytical table with per-market labels, both smoothed-probability classifications, and the k-means comparison columns because that is the standard source artifact for all visuals.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In coordination meetings, 'classification table' sounds like an obvious shared object, and both assume the other knows the conventional scope from prior projects; the disagreement is about included fields, not about whether the table exists.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say the 'final figures' will be ready by Thursday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena uses 'final figures' to mean slide-ready visuals with titles, explanatory footnotes, consistent color semantics, and frozen numbering for the client briefing.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: David uses 'final figures' to mean the last analytically approved chart outputs from the code pipeline, even if annotations, branding, and deck placement are still pending.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase is common in research operations and usually passes without clarification; each side assumes the other is using the shop's default meaning, but their defaults come from different functions.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as 'on track' for Friday
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both confirm they are 'on track' for the Friday package.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena believes 'on track' means she can send a largely publication-ready deck by Friday morning with minimal missing polish work.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: David believes 'on track' means the numbers, tables, and chart exports will be stable by Friday, while final visual cleanup can continue later that day.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Status language in coordination meetings is intentionally compressed, and both parties are cooperative; because neither wants to sound obstructive, they accept the positive status label without unpacking the threshold behind it.
